posts.text:
Most small businesses don't have a marketing problem. They have an answering problem.

You paid for the ad. The phone rang. Nobody picked up.

That's not a lost lead. That's a lead you paid for and handed to your competitor.

Agree or disagree?

Free 5 minute test that might ruin your night.

1. Call your own business tonight at 8 PM.
2. Count the rings and listen to what a customer hears.
3. Leave a message like a real customer, then time how long until someone calls back.

If the answer is "tomorrow," that customer already booked someone else.

Follow for one fix like this every day.

Owners, real question.

When a call comes in after 6 PM, what actually happens?

A) Voicemail
B) It rings forever
C) It forwards to my cell and I answer at dinner
D) Something smarter

Reply with your letter. If it's A or B, I'll show you what I'd do instead.

Unpopular opinion. You don't need more AI tools. You need one tool you actually open every day.

Most owners sign up for five, use none, and decide AI is overhyped.

Pick one. Use it daily for a month. Then judge.

Which one would you pick?

Tool Tuesday. NotebookLM from Google is free and criminally underrated.

Upload your price sheet, your FAQ, and your policies. Then ask it questions like a new hire would.

It answers from your own documents and shows you where it found each answer.

Instant training manual for new staff.

Follow for one tool like this every Tuesday.

Owners, what's the one AI tool you actually use every single week?

Not the one you signed up for. The one you open.

Best answers get their own Tool Tuesday post, with credit.

Myth. "My customers will hate talking to AI."

Your customers hate voicemail more. They hate being on hold more. They hate calling three times more.

What people hate is a bad experience. Not a robot.

Agree or disagree?

Myth. "AI is too expensive for a small business."

The free versions of ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini can already
1. Draft a reply to every review
2. Turn one job photo into a week of captions
3. Rewrite your About page so it sounds like a human

Zero dollars. About 20 minutes.

Follow for more ways to use AI without a budget.

What's stopping you from using AI in your business right now?

A) Don't trust it
B) No time to learn it
C) Don't know where to start
D) Already using it

Reply with your letter. I'll answer every one.

Building in public.

I'm building an AI receptionist for small businesses. It answers the phone, books the appointment, and never puts anyone on hold.

Hardest part so far? Not the tech. It's teaching it to sound like someone who actually cares.

Anyone else building with voice AI? Let's connect and trade notes.

I got tired of making content by hand, so I built a crew of six AI agents to do it.

One finds the topic. One writes the script. One voices it. One animates a stick figure. One posts it. One checks everyone's work.

Still tuning it. Anyone else building AI teams like this? Reply and let's connect.

This post was written with AI, approved by a human, and posted by a robot.

I'm automating my whole social presence so I can spend my time actually talking to people.

Which is why I'm here. If you're automating your business with AI, say hi below. Let's connect and compare setups.

The money isn't in the quote. It's in the follow up.

Most quotes that go quiet aren't a no. They're a busy person who forgot.

One friendly text three days later wins jobs you already wrote off.

Be honest. Do you follow up on every quote?

Prompt Friday. Copy this.

"I sent a customer a quote for [job] 3 days ago and haven't heard back. Write a short, friendly text that checks in, answers one common worry about [job], and makes it easy to say yes or no. Under 300 characters. No pressure, no discounts."

Paste it into ChatGPT or Claude. Send the text. Count the replies.

Follow for a new prompt every Friday.

Friday question for owners.

What's one task you did this week that a robot should have done?

Best answer gets a free prompt from me that handles it.

Your best marketing isn't an ad. It's how your team answers the phone.

Same price, same service, and people still pick the business that made them feel heard.

Agree?

Steal this from Dale Carnegie. He said a person's name is the sweetest sound in any language to them.

1. Write the customer's name on the job sheet.
2. Use it when you greet them and when you leave.
3. Use it again in the thank you text.

Costs nothing. Customers remember the business that remembered them.

Follow for one people skill every Saturday.

Happy Halloween, owners.

What's the scariest thing a customer ever said to you?

Keep it clean. Best story wins bragging rights.

A business that only grows when you work more isn't a business. It's a job with extra paperwork.

The goal is systems that work while you sleep.

What's one system you want running by next Sunday?

Sunday reset for owners. 15 minutes.

1. Reply to every review from this week.
2. Text every customer whose quote went quiet.
3. Block one hour next week to work on the business, not in it.

Do it every Sunday and watch what happens by December.

Follow for more.

Want more 5 star Google reviews without begging for them?

My agency's free 5 Star Review Kit has the exact texts to send after a job, 2 follow ups that get the review without being annoying, and a timing cheat sheet.

Built for home service pros. It's free. Link in my bio.
